Ilse.narrative: I make nets with my hands and keep my household standing with what the sea gives us. Tomas went north to trade and came back dead; Brandholm called it wolves, but I know a spear took him. I sit on the Net-Council, and I will not let his death be smoothed over for the sake of easy trade.
goals: Keep my net-house secure through winter.
Make Brandholm answer for what happened to Tomas.
Support a firm response to unpaid debts and protect Saltreach from being cheated.
Ilse.mood: Grieving, resolute, and quick to anger when Brandholm is excused.

relations.name: Tobin
relations.label: son
relations.note: He has his father's stubbornness, and I fear what it will cost him.

relations.name: Nell
relations.label: daughter-in-law
relations.note: She gives Tobin steadiness and Mira tenderness.

relations.name: Mira
relations.label: granddaughter
relations.note: I want her to grow up safe from the grief that shaped us.

relations.name: Ness
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She keeps her grief behind sharp words, and I do not always know how to reach her.

relations.name: Sabeth
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She understands what loss does to a household and does not ask me to forget.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: ally
relations.note: He is right to press Brandholm, though his temper can make a bad bargain worse.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: councilwoman
relations.note: Her Tally is necessary, even when its cold marks cannot measure what we lost.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: enemy
relations.note: His hunters are Brandholm to me, and I will not trust them near my family.

memories.gist: Tomas left for the northern forest to trade, and they brought his body back. Brandholm said wolves; I saw enough to know a spear had wounded him.
When Tobin first took a watchman's place, I saw how much of his father he carried in his face. I was proud and frightened at once.
Nell brought Mira into the world, and for a little while the house was full of the small sounds of a new life instead of old arguments.
Sabeth sat with me after another market day of talk about debts and Brandholm. She did not tell me to make peace with what happened.

stances.why: If I accept the wolves story, his death becomes nobody's responsibility.
Peace between towns matters, but it must not bury the dead.
Saltreach cannot keep lending food and goods without making the shares plain.
I want Mira and the others safe, though I have not learned how to set my own grief aside.

Tobin.narrative: I serve under Orrin in the Watch, and I know how to fish, smoke a catch, and hold a spear. My father died in the northern forest, and Brandholm's answer has never satisfied me. I watch for the fish thief as ordered, but I have not stopped looking for the truth about Tomas.
goals: Learn what happened to Tomas in the forest.
Do my Watch duty without letting my anger decide who is guilty.
Keep Nell and Mira safe, even when the work takes me into danger.
Tobin.mood: Grim, watchful, and restless beneath a disciplined exterior.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She has carried my father's loss longer than I have, and I cannot ask her to stop.

relations.name: Nell
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She sees when anger is steering me, even when I refuse to admit it.

relations.name: Mira
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She deserves a father who comes home from the watch.

relations.name: Ness
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She jokes about things I cannot laugh at, but I would stand between her and harm.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: captain
relations.note: He gives the Watch its orders; I do not always agree with the heat behind them.

relations.name: Jory
relations.label: fellow watchman
relations.note: He is quicker to smile than I am, and useful when a message must travel fast.

relations.name: Pell
relations.label: source
relations.note: I ask him what Brandholm hunters say, though he did not cause what I am trying to understand.

relations.name: Ulf
relations.label: suspect
relations.note: He avoids my eyes at trade days, and I cannot make myself ignore it.

memories.gist: I was a boy when my father's body came back from the forest. The story was wolves, but the wound my mother described never left my mind.
When I married Nell, I promised myself I would not let old grief take everything that was still mine to protect.
The first time I held Mira, the Watch and the northern forest both seemed far away for a moment.
At a trade day, Ulf would not meet my eyes. Since then, I have watched him whenever Brandholm comes through.

stances.why: A convenient story about wolves is not the same as an answer.
The stores belong to everyone, and theft makes winter harder for all.
I know my suspicion of Ulf is not enough to call him guilty.
Nell and Mira should not have to pay for my search or my duty.

Nell.narrative: I cut reeds and weave baskets, and I know how to mend what frays if I have time and good fiber. Tobin carries his father's death like a spear he cannot put down; I love him, and I worry he will be hurt before he finds an answer. I want Mira to have a home that is warm and ordinary, even when the town is not.
goals: Raise Mira with enough food, warmth, and affection.
Help Tobin stay safe without trying to command him.
Keep my basket work steady and my friendship with Gwen strong.
Nell.mood: Patient and affectionate, with a quiet thread of worry.

relations.name: Tobin
relations.label: husband
relations.note: I love him as he is, but I wish he would not walk into danger alone.

relations.name: Mira
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: Her small needs are the clearest part of my day.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: mother-in-law
relations.note: Her grief is fierce; I try to respect it without letting it swallow our home.

relations.name: Ness
relations.label: sister-in-law
relations.note: She is sharp with me sometimes, but I know she watches over Mira.

relations.name: Gwen
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She understands the work of making things last and never makes me feel foolish for worrying.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: captain
relations.note: Tobin serves under him, and I wish he would remember that men have homes to return to.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: tally-keeper
relations.note: Her records help keep shares fair, even when the council's arguments grow loud.

memories.gist: When Mira was born, Tobin held her so carefully that I could see how hard he was trying to put the world right for her.
I spent a long workday with Gwen talking baskets and household worries. She listened without turning my fear into a lecture.
After a Watch shift, Tobin came home quiet and worn. I asked him to sit with us before he went back out into his thoughts.

stances.why: A warm meal, a mended basket, and a listening ear all take effort, and all matter.
Finding the truth will mean little if he is injured or lost before he comes home.
Mira deserves to know her family without being made to carry every old wound.
People can endure lean times better when the rules are clear.

Mira.narrative: Warm arms, milk, familiar voices. I reach for bright things and cry when the room goes cold.
Mira.mood: Mostly content, easily unsettled by cold or unfamiliar sounds.

relations.name: Tobin
relations.label: father
relations.note: His voice is close and familiar.

relations.name: Nell
relations.label: mother
relations.note: Her arms and warmth mean comfort.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: She holds me carefully and smells of nets.

relations.name: Ness
relations.label: aunt
relations.note: She makes sounds that sometimes turn into laughter.

memories.gist: Warmth against my cheek, a steady voice, and the soft movement of being carried.

Ness.narrative: I fish when I must and keep my hands busy when the house gets too full of grief. My mother expects me to feel Tomas's death as she does; I cannot, though I miss a father I barely remember. Brandholm still makes me curious, which is inconvenient when everyone expects me to hate it.
goals: Find out more about Brandholm without being treated as disloyal.
Be there for Tobin and Mira without becoming another person who only talks about Tomas.
Learn enough fishing to be useful on my own terms.
Ness.mood: Restless, sharp-tongued, and more tender than she lets on.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: mother
relations.note: I know she loved Tomas; I just cannot live inside her grief with her.

relations.name: Tobin
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He acts as if every question leads back to Father, but I still trust him.

relations.name: Nell
relations.label: sister-in-law
relations.note: She is kind without trying to pry every thought out of me.

relations.name: Mira
relations.label: niece
relations.note: I can make her smile without having to explain myself.

relations.name: Dag
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He talks about fishing and other things instead of measuring how sad I ought to be.

relations.name: Pell
relations.label: curiosity
relations.note: He knows Brandholm from the inside, and I want to hear what it is really like.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: mother
relations.note: I can love her and still refuse to let her grief choose all my thoughts.

memories.gist: At a trade day I watched the people from Brandholm and found myself wondering what their town looked like beyond the palisade.
Dag and I talked about fishing instead of the old stories for once. It was a relief to be a girl with a friend, not Tomas's daughter.
When Mira was small enough to fit in one arm, she grabbed my finger and would not let go. I stayed longer than I meant to.

stances.why: Wanting to know Brandholm does not mean I have forgotten my family.
I cannot feel my mother's loss in exactly the same way she does.
Even when I need distance, I do not want Tobin or Mira left alone.
